_doc: The match racket, an original design: the invented Ostrel Keystone, a diamond-shaped power racket (GDD 2: solid, perforated face, at most 455 mm long and 260 mm wide; GDD 10: rackets of invented designs). Metres in the racket's own axes: X across the face, Z along the racket from the butt (-0.075) to the tip, Y through the face, grip centre on the origin (Tools/AssetPipeline/README.md). Read by asset_lib/racket_layout.py, asset_lib/racket_textures.py and blender/build_racket.py; colours are in palette.json 'racket'. See docs/decisions/0008-racket.md.

brand._doc: Invented brand and model, searched before use (no padel brand, racket line or product with either name). The wordmark is drawn from the stroke letters in racket_textures.py, no font files.
brand.name: OSTREL

frame._doc: thickness_m is the regulation maximum of 38 mm. edge_radius_m rounds every edge of the frame, the heart and the throat (Blender curve bevel). The outline is the right half (x >= 0) from the tip down to the neck, in metres, smoothed by a Catmull-Rom spline and mirrored; it is the finished edge, and the builder insets it by edge_radius_m before bevelling. The widest point sits at about two thirds of the head's height, which is what makes it a diamond (head-heavy, power) rather than a round (control) or teardrop. The tip sits bumper.proud_m below 0.38 so that, with the bumper on, the racket is exactly 455 mm long.
frame._face_margin: How far in from the edge the hitting face starts: the frame's own width as seen on the face. No holes in it.
frame._neck: The frame runs on into the handle down to neck_z_m, hidden under the grip, so the grip's finishing tape always covers where they meet.

heart._doc: An open heart: two windows either side of a central bridge, between the throat arms and the bottom of the face. arm_width_m is each arm's width across, bridge_width_m the bridge's; top_z_m is the window top on the centre line, top_rise the slope it rises by towards the arms. Every window corner is rounded to about corner_radius_m. The bridge must stay wider than twice frame.edge_radius_m, or the two windows' bevels would meet inside it.

holes._doc: Through-holes in the face (regulation diameter 9 to 13 mm). The pattern is original: an outer ring that follows the face's own diamond outline, ring_insets_m in from the face edge and spaced pitch_m apart, then a staggered grid (grid_pitch_m, rows from grid_top_z_m down) filling the middle. Always left-right symmetric, never closer than min_gap_m edge to edge, and none where the wordmark panel is (keep_clear_z_m). Holes also stay graphic_clear_m above the paint panel's edge, so the wordmark panel stays whole; the keystone is printed and drilled through, like most real face graphics.
holes._lod_segments: Segments per hole at LOD0, LOD1 and LOD2. 0: no geometry; the face material darkens the hole from T_Racket_Masks.A instead, which from the broadcast camera reads the same.

bumper._doc: Rubber protector over the top of the frame, from the tip down to start_deg either side (0 is the tip), proud of the frame by proud_m and wrapping onto the faces by wrap_m.

weights._doc: The adjustable-weight look: an alloy cartridge set into the bridge on both faces, with two hex screws, and an alloy port in each shoulder of the frame at the widest point. Cosmetic only: the racket's mass and balance live in Data/ with the shot model.

grip._doc: Elliptical handle under a white overgrip. semi_axes_m is (across X, through Y): about 118 mm round with the overgrip, a mid-size padel grip, and just larger than the frame's neck (33 x 38 mm) that runs inside it. The wrap is a helix of overlapping bands (pitch_m apart, raised by step_m at each overlap). The finishing tape sits at the top of the wrap, the butt cap at the bottom.
grip._lod_segments: Around x along the wrap. LOD0 carries the helix; the lower LODs are plain ellipses.

textures._doc: T_Racket_Masks covers a square of the face, size_m on a side, centred on X = 0 with its top edge at the tip: R paint, G accent, B ink (the wordmark and the fine print), A holes (so LOD2 shows them without geometry). T_CarbonWeave_Mask is one tile of 2x2 twill carbon, tiled every weave_tile_m. T_RacketGrit_N is one tile of the raised sand finish that gives the face its grip on the ball (the '3D' texture), tiled every grit_tile_m.

graphics._doc: The original face graphic, in face metres. A keystone (the wedge-shaped top stone of an arch) outlined in the accent colour round the sweet spot; a paint panel across the lower head, cut by a rising diagonal, carrying the wordmark; an accent pinstripe pinstripe_inset_m inside the edge. Text heights are cap heights.
